subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB328, LANDED. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode': OK, 16)): 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode. If the file does not support those statements, the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to '37' and the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful. The successful execution of an OPEN statement with the I-O phrase sets the open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 to open in the I-O mode.' TWO halves. HALF 2 (the open mode is set) was already conforming: FileConnector.Open assigns Mode and sets _openMode from the success family. HALF 1 (the '37') was the defect. WAS: the only producer of '37' for a write-incapable file was the shared catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) around OpenCore, which fired for SEQUENTIAL only because that organization's I-O and EXTEND arms open write-capable streams; the relative and indexed I-O arms merely Attach() (a READ of the store), so writability was never probed. Probed on a worktree build at 17c11fd4 with three files created by the compiler and then made read-only (a real host attribute, not a simulation): OPEN I-O answered SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' on the SAME condition; the keyed successes were then believed downstream (READ '00', REWRITE '00') and the loss surfaced only as a '30' at CLOSE on a file whose MD5 was unchanged. The identical omission made OPEN EXTEND answer SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' where 9.1.13.6 6) a) 1. requires '37' (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the EXTEND or OUTPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support write operations': OK, 6) a) 1.); OPEN OUTPUT was already '37' on all three because its keyed arm eagerly calls RecordFraming.WriteStore. NOW: the write-capability question is an OPEN-CONTRACT question, asked ONCE above the organizations. HostFile.PermitsWrite (IO/FileSupport.cs) asks the host for a writable handle (FileMode.Open + FileAccess.Write + FileShare.ReadWrite, nothing written) and answers false only on UnauthorizedAccessException; every other IOException propagates so 9.1.13.6 1)'s '30' stays mapped in the one place. FileConnector.Open calls it for I-O, EXTEND and OUTPUT on a Present file, after GR10's '39' and before OpenCore, so every organization -- including one added later -- inherits the answer instead of re-earning it. GR16 names no organization and Table 20 is why it cannot: REWRITE sits under the I-O column for sequential, random AND dynamic access, so 'supports the statements permitted in the I-O mode' entails write capability whatever the organization. RE-PROBED after the fix on the same three read-only files: OPEN I-O 37/37/37, OPEN EXTEND 37/37/37, OPEN OUTPUT 37/37/37 -- nine cells. OVER-FIRE MEASURED, not assumed: the same read-only files still OPEN INPUT '00' and READ their record on all three organizations (a read-only file supports everything Table 20 permits in the input mode), and a WRITABLE file still opens I-O '00' and rewrites on all three. GR25 ('If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, the file is not affected', cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK, 25)) holds through the probe: content MD5 and last-write time are identical after the refused open. INPUT IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE PROBE and the exclusion is required, not an optimization -- probing write for INPUT would refuse an OPEN the operating environment carries out perfectly, and 9.1.13.6 6) a) 3.'s read-capability question is answered by the organization's own eager read (measured on all three: see GR-9.1.13.6-6). BOTH HALVES OF GR16 ARE COVERED, not just the one that was defective: the rule says the file must support the input AND output statements the I-O mode permits, and Table 20 lists READ under the I-O column beside REWRITE, so a file this process may WRITE but not READ is equally '37'. Measured with icacls /deny :(RD) -- read DATA only, so a raw write open still succeeds and HostFile.PermitsWrite accepts the file -- OPEN I-O answered '37' on sequential, relative and indexed, produced by the organization's own eager read rather than by the write probe; unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests.OpenIo_PresentAndWritableButNotReadable_Is37 asserts the write-probe premise first so the two halves cannot be confused. COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes the precondition for real (a read-only attribute on Windows, mode 0400 on Unix) and verifies it with a RAW write open rather than with the subject under test; its nine GR16 cells were shown to FAIL (7 of them -- the four keyed I-O/EXTEND cells, the two keyed OPTIONAL cells and the GR25 inertness assertion) with the check disabled, and the three sequential cells and three OUTPUT cells stayed green, which is exactly the two-arm fingerprint the defect had. unit:HostFileProbeDriftTests keeps the question singular: PermitsWrite is banned outside FileConnector and its call count in the OPEN contract is pinned at one. No conformance golden can reach this arm -- the corpus runner compiles a .cob and compares its output, with nowhere to express 'and first make this file read-only'. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 -- GR16 is version-invariant and docs/CONFORMANCE.md determines the '37' family is emitted at every edition, ungated.
